Subject: Private VPC pricing & support packaging — initial questions

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for yesterday's product walkthrough. A couple of questions came up internally as we try to model commercials for a potential VPC/on-prem engagement:

- How is the platform fee typically amortized for multi-site deployments (we have 3 U.S. sites and one EU site)?
- What levers do you provide to reduce unit costs (e.g., operator licenses, commit vs metered)?
- Can you outline the support tiers and what the SRE/oncall retainer buys (response windows, dedicated pager, runbooks)?

We'd like packaging alternatives to present to our CFO and procurement team. If you have a simple matrix (starter / scale / enterprise) plus a recommended concession framework, that would help.

Also attaching our procurement intake form (Procurement_Form_GH.pdf) — happy to fill anything else.

Best,

GrowthHealth

Subject: Re: Private VPC pricing & support packaging — initial questions

Hi Lina — great to meet you yesterday. Thanks for the clear list. High level answers below and I attached a short "packaging at a glance" PDF and the pricing model workbook.

Summary (quick):
- Packaging options:
  1) Starter: single-site pilot, low platform fee, metered usage, standard business-hours support.
  2) Scale: multi-site bundle (3 sites), amortized platform fee, committed throughput (preferred), priority SLAs + SRE retainer.
  3) Enterprise (multi-region): full amortization across sites, node/seat operator license mix, 24/7 SRE + dedicated engineer option.

- Platform fee amortization: usually structured over 12 months with a pilot credit for the first 3 months. For multi-site we prorate by active clusters; we can also anchor to committed GPU-hours to reduce fee.

- Cost levers: commit (lowest unit), operator license instead of per-seat, quantization/edge node opt for cost-sensitive paths, caching/batching tuning.

- Support tiers: Standard (business hours, 24-hour ticket SLA), Priority (SLA: 4-hour P1, SRE retainer 40 hrs/mo), Enterprise (SLA: 1-hour P1, 24/7 pager, runbook handoff, onboarding SOW).

I'll ask Dave to call out the SRE/oncall specifics and what our retainer includes. If you can share target commit (GPU-hours) and any regulatory constraints, we can draft two concession scenarios (12-mo commit vs 24-mo commit).

Attachments: GrowthHealth_Packaging_AtAGlance.pdf (2 pages), VPC_pricing_model.xlsx

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Principal Sales — Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

Date: Tue, 17 Aug 2026 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Private VPC pricing & support packaging — SRE/oncall detail

Hi Lina — quick technical note to add to Marissa's overview.

SRE retainer & oncall coverage (what it buys):
- Runbook creation + handover: up to 40 hours during onboarding for Scale / Enterprise packages.
- Pager rotation: Priority tier gets our shared oncall with 4-hr P1 response; Enterprise gets dedicated pager slices and an escalation engineer during business hours.
- Dedicated engineer option: optional add-on (0.2–1.0 FTE equivalence) for high-change environments.
- Incident RCA & playbooks: two post-incident RCAs per year included for Enterprise.

Operational clarifications:
- Implementation credit can be applied to onboarding engineering hours (we invoice separately from platform fee).
- For multi-site: network egress concerns — we recommend a per-region private peer + one cross-region replication lane to keep costs predictable.

Sharing the pricing workbook (VPC_pricing_model.xlsx) with detailed line items — please ping if you want a walkthrough with our solutions team.

Thanks,
David Kim
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Proposed headline (12-month commit, 600 GPU-hrs/mo baseline):
- Platform fee: 8% discount off list for year 1 (applied monthly).
- Implementation credit: $30,000 one-time (applied against onboarding bill).
- Support: Priority tier included for first 6 months, then re-evaluate based on usage.
- Pilot terms: 3-month pilot with a 50% platform fee credit for pilot months (then true-up on conversion). Pilot can convert to the 12-month committed agreement with a signed SOW.

If you need a deeper discount, we can consider a 24-month commit or an increased committed GPU floor. Please let me know Lina / procurement if $30k + 8% is acceptable — that would let us draft a short SOW and pre-fill DocuSign for review.

Hi Lina / Procurement team — thanks for the patience while we aligned internally. Final concession framework we can commit to in writing (pending SOW sign):

1) Commercials (12-mo commit, baseline 600 GPU-hrs/mo):
   - Platform fee: 8% credit applied month-over-month for first 12 months.
   - Implementation credit: $25,000 one-time, applied to onboarding engineering invoice.
   - Pilot: 3-month pilot available. For pilot months we will apply a 50% platform fee credit; if you convert within 30 days of pilot completion the pilot credit is replaced by the 8% annual credit (no double-dipping).

2) Support & SRE:
   - Priority tier included for first 6 months (SRE retainer: 40 hrs/mo).
   - Option to add a Dedicated Engineer (0.4 FTE equivalent) at a fixed monthly rate thereafter.

3) Expansion mechanics:
   - True-up cadence quarterly; additional sites/nodes are added to the committed baseline at next quarter's billing cycle.
   - If you expand beyond 3x baseline GPU-hours we will re-evaluate discount banding (good-faith negotiation).

Additional notes: We will deliver a draft SOW (Redwood_SOW_Draft.docx) and a pre-filled DocuSign (link below) for review. If GrowthHealth signs a 24-month commitment we can increase the platform fee credit to 12% and raise the implementation credit to $40k.
